digest.component_or_area: DC comment and description convergence testing
propositions: DC lacks convergence test suites for oversized comments and descriptions, unlike Cloud which has incident-hardened suites that verify truncated values read back identically on a second pass.

DC's comment sanitizer is bound to WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32767) via a shared constant and fitter, but the binding's provenance is undocumented; it should cite jira.text.field.character.limit property and JRASERVER-28519 which establish 32767 as the documented default for both descriptions and comments.

Tests driven through compute_outbound_mutations or _diff_comments without explicit injection of DC-specific backends fall back to Cloud's configuration via select_backend(load_config()), silently testing Cloud behavior while reporting DC coverage.

A DC comment convergence test cannot use value-based assertions to prove it exercised DC's sanitizer, because DC and Cloud truncate at identical limits (32767) and append byte-identical suffixes; it must instead verify identity or record that the injected DC sanitizer instance was invoked.

A DC description convergence test can use value-based assertions because DC fits plain characters at WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32767) while Cloud fits ADF-serialized size at _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32000), a genuine and measurable difference between the two backends.
